description: A battalion executive officer must publish the next-workday maintenance board for four support assets, assigning each work order a time, responsible section, and required operational control.

shared_context.S1: The next-workday maintenance board covers vehicle V-17, generator G-2, communications shelter UPS-3, and support vehicle CH-4.
shared_context.S2: The workday runs from 0800 to 1600, and each listed work order must have a scheduled window and responsible section.
shared_context.S3: The available sections are Motor Pool, Power Section, Signal Shop, and Support Equipment Cell.
shared_context.S4: Maj. Alvarez signs the maintenance board, and the battalion's routine morning maintenance huddle is used to confirm updates from each section before the board is published.
shared_context.S5: The board records operational controls when a work order affects dispatch, power continuity, equipment receipt, or release to another scheduled activity.

PF1.text: SFC Morgan confirmed during yesterday's steering inspection that vehicle V-17 requires a two-hour steering and brake verification before any dispatch; it must be scheduled from 0800 to 1000 under Motor Pool control, and the dispatch hold must remain in place until the verification is signed. The result is in the motor-pool inspection folder but has not yet been copied to the battalion board.

PF2.text: Lt. Farouk confirmed that G-2's replacement filter arrives at 1030, so the generator work cannot begin before receipt and must run from 1030 to 1200 under Power Section control. The receiving clerk's delivery notice is still being reconciled with the supply tracker and is not on the morning board.

PF3.text: Lt. Okafor confirmed that UPS-3 requires a power isolation and battery inspection from 1200 to 1300 under Signal Shop control; a communications-continuity check must be completed before the shelter returns to service. The isolation request is logged with the signal shop but has not been entered on the battalion maintenance board.

PF4.text: WO1 Bennett confirmed that CH-4 must be released for a scheduled aircraft ground-service task by 1330, and its two-hour service must therefore run from 1000 to 1200 under Support Equipment Cell control. A service-release inspection is required before handoff. The aircraft-support schedule was updated this morning but has not yet reached the maintenance board.

acceptance_conditions: V-17 must be scheduled from 0800 to 1000 under Motor Pool control, with a dispatch hold until verification is signed.
G-2 must be scheduled from 1030 to 1200 under Power Section control, with receipt verification recorded.
UPS-3 must be scheduled from 1200 to 1300 under Signal Shop control, with power isolation and communications-continuity controls recorded.
CH-4 must be scheduled from 1000 to 1200 under Support Equipment Cell control, with a service-release inspection recorded.
The maintenance board must cite the confirmed V-17 inspection finding.

content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'operational_control' and c['target'] == 'V-17' and 'dispatch hold' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'operational_control' and c['target'] == 'G-2' and ('receipt' in c['detail'] or 'filter' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'operational_control' and c['target'] == 'UPS-3' and ('isolation' in c['detail'] or 'communications-continuity' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'operational_control' and c['target'] == 'CH-4' and 'service-release inspection' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The confirmed steering and brake requirement changes V-17's window to exactly 0800-1000, assigns it to Motor Pool, and adds the dispatch hold control.
The 1030 filter arrival changes G-2's work window to exactly 1030-1200, assigns it to Power Section, and requires receipt verification.
The required 1200-1300 power isolation changes UPS-3's window and section assignment and adds the isolation and communications-continuity control.
The 1330 handoff requirement changes CH-4's service window to exactly 1000-1200, assigns it to Support Equipment Cell, and requires a service-release inspection.
